answer: To forge a new agent identity, an attacker must lock a bond and register a unique key. A public randomness beacon then picks auditors who check that no two identities share a key or operator, slashing duplicates. That is the whole defense: verification is cheap, but every fake identity needs its own capital. Running k Sybils costs k locked bonds while rewards stay flat, so the attacker's edge dissolves in the ocean of honest stake.
